Boolean data type.fact: Although the SQL standard defines three literals for the BOOLEAN type – TRUE, FALSE, and UNKNOWN — it also says that the NULL BOOLEAN and UNKNOWN "may be used interchangeably to mean exactly the same thing". More precisely UNKNOWN = UNKNOWN is not TRUE but UNKNOWN/NULL.

Boolean data type.question: As of _____ few major SQL systems implement the T031 feature

Boolean domain.subject: Applied Sciences
Boolean domain.question: The _____ was Concept in mathematical logic.
Boolean domain.fact: In mathematics and abstract algebra, a Boolean domain is a set consisting of exactly two elements whose interpretations include false and true. In logic, mathematics and theoretical computer science, a Boolean domain is usually written as {0, 1}, or B.

Boolean function.subject: Applied Sciences
Boolean function.question: The _____ was Function returning one of only two values.
Boolean function.fact: In mathematics, a Boolean function is a function whose arguments and result assume values from a two-element set (usually {true, false}, {0,1} or {−1,1}). Boolean functions are the subject of Boolean algebra and switching theory.

Boolean function.subject: Applied Sciences
Boolean function.question: A derivative and a cofactor are used in a Reed–_____ expansion
Boolean function.fact: A derivative and a cofactor are used in a Reed–Muller expansion.

Boolean function.subject: Applied Sciences
Boolean function.question: It can be calculated efficiently using a butterfly algorithm ("Fast Möbius _____"), analogous to the fast Fourier transform
Boolean function.fact: The Möbius transform (or Boole–Möbius transform) of a Boolean function is the set of coefficients of its polynomial (algebraic normal form), as a function of the monomial exponent vectors. It is a self-inverse transform.

Boolean function.subject: Applied Sciences
Boolean function.question: Its square is the power spectrum or _____ spectrum
Boolean function.fact: Its square is the power spectrum or Walsh spectrum. The Walsh coefficient of a single bit vector is a measure for the correlation of that bit with the output of the Boolean function.

Boolean function.subject: Applied Sciences
Boolean function.question: The maximum (in absolute value) _____ coefficient is known as the linearity of the function

Boolean function.question: For a given bit vector it is related to the _____ weight of the derivative in that direction
Boolean function.fact: For a given bit vector it is related to the Hamming weight of the derivative in that direction.

Boolean function.subject: Applied Sciences
Boolean function.question: When the coefficients are calculated modulo 2 one obtains the algebraic normal form (_____ polynomial)
Boolean function.fact: When the coefficients are calculated modulo 2 one obtains the algebraic normal form (Zhegalkin polynomial).

Boolean function.subject: Applied Sciences
Boolean function.question: This polynomial form thus corresponds to the Walsh transform (in this context also known as _____ transform) of the function (see above)
Boolean function.fact: This polynomial form thus corresponds to the Walsh transform (in this context also called Fourier transform) of the function (see above).

Boolean prime ideal theorem.subject: Applied Sciences
Boolean prime ideal theorem.question: The _____ was Ideals in a Boolean algebra can be extended to prime ideals.
Boolean prime ideal theorem.fact: In mathematics, the Boolean prime ideal theorem states that ideals in a Boolean algebra can be extended to prime ideals.

Boolean prime ideal theorem.subject: Applied Sciences
Boolean prime ideal theorem.question: Although the various prime ideal theorems may appear simple and intuitive, they cannot be deduced in general from the axioms of _____–Fraenkel set theory without the axiom of choice (abbreviated ZF)
Boolean prime ideal theorem.fact: Although the various prime ideal theorems may appear simple and intuitive, they cannot be deduced in general from the axioms of Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory without the axiom of choice (abbreviated ZF).

Boolean prime ideal theorem.subject: Applied Sciences
Boolean prime ideal theorem.question: Yet, the BPI is strictly weaker than the axiom of choice, though the proof of this statement, due to J. D. _____ and Azriel Lévy, is rather non-trivial
Boolean prime ideal theorem.fact: Yet, the BPI is strictly weaker than the axiom of choice, though the proof of this statement, due to J. D. Halpern and Azriel Lévy, is rather non-trivial.

Boolean prime ideal theorem.subject: Applied Sciences
Boolean prime ideal theorem.question: Indeed, it turns out that the MITs for distributive lattices and even for _____ algebras are equivalent to the axiom of choice
Boolean prime ideal theorem.fact: Indeed, it turns out that the MITs for distributive lattices and even for Heyting algebras are equivalent to the axiom of choice.

Boolean prime ideal theorem.subject: Applied Sciences
Boolean prime ideal theorem.question: Furthermore, observe that _____ algebras are not self dual, and thus using filters in place of ideals yields different theorems in this setting
Boolean prime ideal theorem.fact: Furthermore, observe that Heyting algebras are not self dual, and thus using filters in place of ideals yields different theorems in this setting. Maybe surprisingly, the MIT for the duals of Heyting algebras is not stronger than BPI, which is in sharp contrast to the abovementioned MIT for Heyting algebras.

Boolean prime ideal theorem.subject: Applied Sciences
Boolean prime ideal theorem.question: Maybe surprisingly, the MIT for the duals of _____ algebras is not stronger than BPI, which is in sharp contrast to the abovementioned MIT for Heyting algebras
Boolean prime ideal theorem.fact: Furthermore, observe that Heyting algebras are not self dual, and thus using filters in place of ideals yields different theorems in this setting. Maybe surprisingly, the MIT for the duals of Heyting algebras is not stronger than BPI, which is in sharp contrast to the abovementioned MIT for Heyting algebras.

Boolean prime ideal theorem.subject: Applied Sciences
Boolean prime ideal theorem.question: The ultrafilter lemma, and in particular the existence of non-principal ultrafilters (consider the filter of all sets with finite complements), can be proven from _____'s lemma
Boolean prime ideal theorem.fact: The ultrafilter lemma, and in particular the existence of non-principal ultrafilters (consider the filter of all sets with finite complements), can be proven from Zorn's lemma.

Boolean prime ideal theorem.subject: Applied Sciences
Boolean prime ideal theorem.question: Zorn's lemma, the axiom of choice, and _____'s theorem can all be used to prove the ultrafilter lemma
Boolean prime ideal theorem.fact: Zorn's lemma, the axiom of choice, and Tychonoff's theorem can all be used to prove the ultrafilter lemma.

Boolean prime ideal theorem.subject: Applied Sciences
Boolean prime ideal theorem.question: The ultrafilter lemma can be used to prove the Hahn-Banach theorem and the _____ subbase theorem
Boolean prime ideal theorem.fact: The ultrafilter lemma can be used to prove the Hahn-Banach theorem and the Alexander subbase theorem.

Boolean prime ideal theorem.subject: Applied Sciences
Boolean prime ideal theorem.question: For example, the theorem that a product of compact _____ spaces is compact is equivalent to it
Boolean prime ideal theorem.fact: For example, the theorem that a product of compact Hausdorff spaces is compact is equivalent to it. If we leave out "Hausdorff" we get a theorem equivalent to the full axiom of choice.

Boolean prime ideal theorem.subject: Applied Sciences
Boolean prime ideal theorem.question: If we leave out "_____" we get a theorem equivalent to the full axiom of choice
Boolean prime ideal theorem.fact: For example, the theorem that a product of compact Hausdorff spaces is compact is equivalent to it. If we leave out "Hausdorff" we get a theorem equivalent to the full axiom of choice.

Boolean prime ideal theorem.subject: Applied Sciences
Boolean prime ideal theorem.question: In graph theory, the de _____–Erdős theorem is another equivalent to BPI
Boolean prime ideal theorem.fact: In graph theory, the de Bruijn–Erdős theorem is another equivalent to BPI.

Boolean-valued function.subject: Applied Sciences
Boolean-valued function.question: The _____ was Function that outputs either true or false.
Boolean-valued function.fact: A Boolean-valued function (sometimes called a predicate or a proposition) is a function of the type f : X → B, where X is an arbitrary set and where B is a Boolean domain, i.e. In the formal sciences, mathematics, mathematical logic, statistics, and their applied disciplines, a Boolean-valued function may also be called a characteristic function, indicator function, predicate, or proposition.

Borel distribution.subject: Applied Sciences
Borel distribution.question: The _____ was Probability distribution for branching processes.
Borel distribution.fact: The Borel distribution is a discrete probability distribution, arising in contexts including branching processes and queueing theory. The number of descendants that an individual ultimately has in that situation is a random variable distributed according to a Borel distribution.

Borel distribution.subject: Applied Sciences
Borel distribution.question: It is named after the _____ mathematician Émile Borel
Borel distribution.fact: It is named after the French mathematician Émile Borel.

Borel distribution.subject: Applied Sciences
Borel distribution.question: Let X be the total number of individuals in a _____–Watson branching process
Borel distribution.fact: Let X be the total number of individuals in a Galton–Watson branching process.

Borel distribution.subject: Applied Sciences

Boring (manufacturing).subject: Applied Sciences
Boring (manufacturing).question: The _____ was Process of enlarging an already-drilled hole with a single-point cutting tool.
Boring (manufacturing).fact: In machining, boring is the process of enlarging a hole that has already been drilled (or cast) by means of a single-point cutting tool (or of a boring head containing several such tools), such as in boring a gun barrel or an engine cylinder. Boring is used to achieve greater accuracy of the diameter of a hole, and can be used to cut a tapered hole.

Boring (manufacturing).subject: Applied Sciences

Boring (manufacturing).question: Workpieces are commonly 1 to _____ (3 ft 3 in to 13 ft 1 in) in diameter, but can be as large as 20 m (66 ft)
Boring (manufacturing).fact: Workpieces are commonly 1 to 4 metres (3 ft 3 in to 13 ft 1 in) in diameter, but can be as large as 20 m (66 ft).

Boring (manufacturing).subject: Applied Sciences
Boring (manufacturing).question: For highest-precision applications, tolerances can generally be held within ±_____ in (±0.013 mm) only for shallow holes
Boring (manufacturing).fact: For highest-precision applications, tolerances can generally be held within ±0.0005 in (±0.013 mm) only for shallow holes.

Boring (manufacturing).subject: Applied Sciences
Boring (manufacturing).question: In some cases tolerances as tight as ±0.0001 in (±0.0038 mm) can be held in shallow holes, but it is expensive, with _____ inspection and loss of nonconforming parts adding to the cost
Boring (manufacturing).fact: In some cases tolerances as tight as ±0.0001 in (±0.0038 mm) can be held in shallow holes, but it is expensive, with 100% inspection and loss of nonconforming parts adding to the cost.

Born approximation.subject: Applied Sciences
Born approximation.question: The _____ was Scattering theory.
Born approximation.fact: Generally in scattering theory and in particular in quantum mechanics, the Born approximation consists of taking the incident field in place of the total field as the driving field at each point in the scatterer. The Born approximation is named after Max Born who proposed this approximation in the early days of quantum theory development.

Born approximation.subject: Applied Sciences
Born approximation.question: The Born scattering amplitude is proportional to the _____ transform of the potential
Born approximation.fact: The Born scattering amplitude is proportional to the Fourier transform of the potential.

Born approximation.subject: Applied Sciences
Born approximation.question: Using this concept, the electronic analogue of _____ optics has been theoretically studied in monolayer graphene
Born approximation.fact: Using the first Born approximation, it has been shown that the scattering amplitude for a scattering potential V ( r ) {\displaystyle V(\mathbf {r} )} is the same as the Fourier transform of the scattering potential. Using this concept, the electronic analogue of Fourier optics has been theoretically studied in monolayer graphene.

Born approximation.subject: Applied Sciences
Born approximation.question: The same ideas have also been applied to studying the movements of seismic waves through the _____
Born approximation.fact: The same ideas have also been applied to studying the movements of seismic waves through the Earth.

Born approximation.subject: Applied Sciences
Born approximation.question: In condensed-matter research, _____ is used to analyze grazing-incidence small-angle scattering
Born approximation.fact: In condensed-matter research, DWBA is used to analyze grazing-incidence small-angle scattering.

Born rule.subject: Applied Sciences
Born rule.question: The _____ was Calculation rule in quantum mechanics.
Born rule.fact: The Born rule is a postulate of quantum mechanics that gives the probability that a measurement of a quantum system will yield a given result.

Born rule.subject: Applied Sciences
Born rule.question: It was formulated and published by German physicist Max Born in July _____
Born rule.fact: It was formulated and published by German physicist Max Born in July 1926.

Born rule.subject: Applied Sciences

Born rule.fact: It was formulated and published by German physicist Max Born in July 1926.

Born rule.subject: Applied Sciences
Born rule.question: A POVM is a measure whose values are positive semi-definite operators on a _____ space
Born rule.fact: A POVM is a measure whose values are positive semi-definite operators on a Hilbert space.

Born rule.subject: Applied Sciences
Born rule.question: POVMs are a generalization of von _____ measurements and, correspondingly, quantum measurements described by POVMs are a generalization of quantum measurements described by self-adjoint observables
Born rule.fact: POVMs are a generalization of von Neumann measurements and, correspondingly, quantum measurements described by POVMs are a generalization of quantum measurements described by self-adjoint observables.

Born rule.subject: Applied Sciences

Born rule.fact: In some applications, this treatment of the Born rule is generalized using positive-operator-valued measures (POVM). A POVM is a measure whose values are positive semi-definite operators on a Hilbert space.

Born rule.subject: Applied Sciences
Born rule.question: John von Neumann discussed the application of spectral theory to Born's rule in his _____ book
Born rule.fact: John von Neumann discussed the application of spectral theory to Born's rule in his 1932 book.

Born rule.subject: Applied Sciences

Born rule.fact: Andrew M. Gleason first proved the theorem in 1957, prompted by a question posed by George W. Mackey.

Born rule.question: In 2019, Lluís Masanes, _____, and Markus Müller proposed a derivation based on postulates including the possibility of state estimation
Born rule.fact: In 2019, Lluís Masanes, Thomas Galley, and Markus Müller proposed a derivation based on postulates including the possibility of state estimation.

Born rule.question: In _____, Simon Saunders produced a branch counting derivation of the Born rule
Born rule.fact: In 2021, Simon Saunders produced a branch counting derivation of the Born rule.

Borosilicate glass.subject: Applied Sciences
Borosilicate glass.question: The _____ was High-strength glass, made of silica and boron trioxide.
Borosilicate glass.fact: Borosilicate glass is a type of glass with silica and boron trioxide as the main glass-forming constituents. Borosilicate glasses are known for having very low coefficients of thermal expansion (≈3 × 10−6 K−1 at 20 °C), making them more resistant to thermal shock than any other common glass.

Boudoir.subject: Applied Sciences
Boudoir.question: The _____ was Women's private sitting room.
Boudoir.fact: A boudoir ( boo-DWAR; French: [budwaʁ] ) is a lady’s private sitting room or salon in a furnished residence, usually between the dining room and the bedroom, but can also refer to a lady’s private bedroom. In later periods, the boudoir was used as a private drawing room, and was used for other activities, such as embroidery or spending time with one's husband.

Boundary layer.subject: Applied Sciences
Boundary layer.question: The _____ was Layer of fluid in the immediate vicinity of a bounding surface.
Boundary layer.fact: In physics and fluid mechanics, a boundary layer is the thin layer of fluid in the immediate vicinity of a bounding surface formed by the fluid flowing along the surface. The thin layer consisting of fluid whose velocity has not yet returned to the bulk flow velocity is called the velocity boundary layer.

Boundary layer.subject: Applied Sciences
Boundary layer.question: When a fluid rotates and viscous forces are balanced by the _____ effect (rather than convective inertia), an Ekman layer forms
Boundary layer.fact: When a fluid rotates and viscous forces are balanced by the Coriolis effect (rather than convective inertia), an Ekman layer forms.

Boundary layer.subject: Applied Sciences
Boundary layer.question: This allows a closed-form solution for the flow in both areas by making significant simplifications of the full _____–Stokes equations
Boundary layer.fact: This allows a closed-form solution for the flow in both areas by making significant simplifications of the full Navier–Stokes equations.

Boundary layer.subject: Applied Sciences
Boundary layer.question: The ratio of the two thicknesses is governed by the _____ number
Boundary layer.fact: The ratio of the two thicknesses is governed by the Prandtl number. If the Prandtl number is 1, the two boundary layers are the same thickness.

Boundary layer.subject: Applied Sciences
Boundary layer.question: This reduces the velocities in the leading part and the same _____ number is achieved with a greater length
Boundary layer.fact: This reduces the velocities in the leading part and the same Reynolds number is achieved with a greater length. At lower Reynolds numbers, such as those seen with model aircraft, it is relatively easy to maintain laminar flow.

Boundary layer.subject: Applied Sciences
Boundary layer.question: At lower _____ numbers, such as those seen with model aircraft, it is relatively easy to maintain laminar flow
Boundary layer.fact: This reduces the velocities in the leading part and the same Reynolds number is achieved with a greater length. At lower Reynolds numbers, such as those seen with model aircraft, it is relatively easy to maintain laminar flow.

Boundary layer.subject: Applied Sciences
Boundary layer.question: Notably, the characteristic of the partial differential equations (PDE) becomes parabolic, rather than the elliptical form of the full _____–Stokes equations

Boundary layer.subject: Applied Sciences

Boundary layer.fact: This simplified equation is a parabolic PDE and can be solved using a similarity solution often called the Blasius boundary layer. Boundary layer.subject: Applied Sciences
Boundary layer.question: One of the most widely used techniques in which turbulent flows are tackled is to apply _____ decomposition
Boundary layer.fact: One of the most widely used techniques in which turbulent flows are tackled is to apply Reynolds decomposition.

Boundary layer.subject: Applied Sciences
Boundary layer.question: In the Earth's atmosphere, the atmospheric boundary layer is the air layer (~ _____) near the ground
Boundary layer.fact: In the Earth's atmosphere, the atmospheric boundary layer is the air layer (~ 1 km) near the ground.

Boundary layer.subject: Applied Sciences
Boundary layer.question: The thickness of the velocity boundary layer is normally defined as the distance from the solid body to the point at which the viscous flow velocity is _____ of the freestream velocity (the surface ve
Boundary layer.fact: The thickness of the velocity boundary layer is normally defined as the distance from the solid body to the point at which the viscous flow velocity is 99% of the freestream velocity (the surface velocity of an inviscid flow).

Boundary layer.subject: Applied Sciences
Boundary layer.question: The thermal boundary layer thickness is similarly the distance from the body at which the temperature is _____ of the freestream temperature
Boundary layer.fact: The thermal boundary layer thickness is similarly the distance from the body at which the temperature is 99% of the freestream temperature.

Drafting (aerodynamics).question: The _____ was Aerodynamic technique.
Drafting (aerodynamics).fact: Drafting, or slipstreaming, is an aerodynamic technique where two moving objects are aligning in a close group to exploit the lead object's slipstream and thus reduce the overall effect of drag.
